```{r setup}
#| echo: false
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggpubr)
library(patchwork)
library(corrr)

source("util/helpers.R")
```

```{r data load}

whoop_master <- readRDS(here("data", "whoop_master.rds"))


# define WHOOP zone colours used consistently across all plots
zone_colours <- c("red" = "#E8453C", "yellow" = "#F5A623", "green" = "#4CAF50")
```


```{r plot-recovery-vs-sleep}
# ── Plot 2: Recovery Score vs Sleep Duration ───────────────
# Scatter plot — each dot = one day
# X axis = how many hours slept that night
# Y axis = recovery score the next morning
# Question: does more sleep = better recovery?

ggplot(whoop_master, aes(x = total_sleep_hours, y = score.recovery_score)) +

  # each dot = one day, coloured by recovery zone
  # alpha = 0.7 makes dots slightly transparent
  # so overlapping dots are still visible
  geom_point(aes(colour = recovery_zone), size = 3, alpha = 0.7) +

  # linear regression trend line (method = "lm")
  # shows the overall direction of the relationship
  # se = TRUE shows grey confidence interval band around the line
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", colour = "grey30",
              se = TRUE, fill = "grey80", linewidth = 1) +
    
  stat_cor(method = "pearson") +

  # use our custom WHOOP zone colours
  scale_colour_manual(values = zone_colours, name = "Recovery Zone") +

  labs(
    title    = "Does More Sleep Lead to Better Recovery?",
    subtitle = "Each dot = one day | Line = trend | Grey band = confidence interval",
    x        = "Total Sleep Hours",
    y        = "Recovery Score (0-100)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    plot.subtitle    = element_text(colour = "grey40", size = 10),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position  = "bottom"
  )
```
-> There is obviously a positive trend between more sleep and higher recovery score.
-> However the correlation coefficient only shows a moderate correlation (R = 0.45)
-> Sleep is not the only factor influencing the recovery for example with a sleep of 7.5 hours the data points Recovery Score Ranges from 100 - 33.

```{r}
# Korrelation Schlaf Tages Strain
ggplot(whoop_master, aes(x = total_deep_sleep_hours, y = score.recovery_score)) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = recovery_zone), size = 3, alpha = 0.7) +
  
   geom_smooth(method = "lm", colour = "grey30",
              se = TRUE, fill = "grey80", linewidth = 1) +
    
  stat_cor(method = "pearson") +

  # use our custom WHOOP zone colours
  scale_colour_manual(values = zone_colours, name = "Recovery Zone") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Korrelation: Tiefschlaf auf Recovery Score",
    x = "Tiefschlaf in Stunden",
    y = "Recovery Score"
  )
```
-> Beachtet man nur den gemessenen Tiefschlaf und seine Korrelation zur Recovery Score sieht man dass die Trendlinie deutlich flacher verläuft (-> Korrelation ist geringer)

```{r}
whoop_master %>%
  correlate()  %>%
  focus(score.recovery_score)  %>%
  arrange(desc(score.recovery_score))
```
-> Schaut sich die Korrelationen an sämtlicher Variablen auf den Recovery Score




-> Gleiches hier 

```{r}
whoop_master |> 
  select(where(is.numeric)) |> 
  select(where(~ sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE) > 0)) |> # Filtert Spalten ohne Varianz heraus
  correlate() |> 
  network_plot(min_cor = 0.2)
```
```{r}
whoop_master |> 
  select(where(is.numeric)) |> 
  select(where(~ sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE) > 0)) |> # Filtert Spalten ohne Varianz heraus
  correlate() |> 
  autoplot() +
  theme_minimal() + # Sie können normale ggplot-Befehle anhängen
  labs(title = "Korrelations-Heatmap mit corrr")
```
